citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
IACUC-approved protocol #23-XX-XXX1 did not provide a written narrative description of the methods and sources used
to determine that alternatives were not available to a procedure that may cause more than momentary pain or distress to
the animals that is included in the protocol (aortic occlusion).
Per this Section, whenever a proposal for animal use contains procedures that may cause more than momentary pain or
distress to the animals, the IACUC shall determine that: (1) the principal investigator has considered alternatives to those
procedures and (2) that the principal investigator has provided a written narrative description of the methods and sources
used to determine that alternatives were not available. These requirements ensure that all procedures contained in the
protocol minimize discomfort, distress, and pain to the animals. The IACUC needs to address this item. Correct by
December 18, 2026.

On August 26, 2026, 13 rabbits covered under an IACUC-approved protocol (#24-XX-XXX1) were removed from this
study by the laboratory as they did not meet the inclusion criteria. The PI staff had used new electrocardiograph (ECG)
equipment to determine the animals met the criteria for the study, without first validating the equipment against manual
recordings prior to its use in the animals. The animals were initially accepted on study based on the measures taken on
the new equipment and later found to not meet the criteria, resulting in animals being on study for longer than was
necessary. The facility must ensure that handling of all animals is done as expeditiously and carefully as possible. The
facility implemented corrective measures prior to the inspection, including more rigorous monitoring and the routine use of
manual calculations.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
